items.headline: Collins (hip) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers and will remain on injured reserve, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
items.summary: Collins isn't quite ready to make his 2026 regular-season debut despite logging a trio of full practices during Week 8 prep. He's been working through a hip injury since training camp, but his ability to practice without restrictions indicates that he's close to being cleared to play. Collins' next chance to play is Week 9 against the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 8.

items.headline: The Falcons signed Jenkins to the practice squad Monday, William McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
items.summary: Jenkins was waived by the Eagles on Thursday, though it didn't take him long to find a new team, albeit as a member of the Falcons' practice squad. The 27-year-old appeared in 16 regular-season games for Philadelphia in the last three seasons but has only one catch during his career.

items.headline: Andrews caught three of four targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 36-10 loss to the Bills.
items.summary: Though Lamar Jackson (ankle) made his long-awaited return to the lineup, his stay lasted just one offensive snap Sunday before he suffered a serious thumb injury. Tyler Huntley then exited the game with a toe injury in the second quarter, forcing undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano into emergency QB duties. No Ravens player produced even 25 receiving yards against Buffalo. Andrews has been in an extended slump and won't be a trustworthy fantasy tight end for Thursday night against the Jaguars.

items.headline: Bateman caught one of three targets for 22 yards in Sunday's 36-10 loss to the Bills.
items.summary: Bateman actually led the Ravens in receiving yards on a day in which three quarterbacks attempted passes for Baltimore. Since posting a 7-88-1 receiving line in Week 2 against the Saints, Bateman has totaled 12 grabs for 200 yards and no scores over his last six games. He has minimal fantasy appeal while Zay Flowers is healthy.

items.headline: Cuevas caught one of two targets for 15 yards during Sunday's 36-10 loss at Buffalo.
items.summary: Cuevas played 13 offensive snaps in Week 8, again trailing behind veteran Mark Andrews (29) and rookie fourth-rounder Matthew Hibner (21). With that said, Cuevas ran routes on most of those snaps, and he drew multiple targets for the fourth straight game Sunday. He still won't be a viable fantasy option in most formats as long as Andrews and Hibner remain healthy.

items.headline: Hibner (hand) was a full participant at practice Thursday.
items.summary: Hibner managed a full practice Thursday for the first time since he hurt his hand back in Week 5 at Atlanta, suggesting he'll more than likely be available in Week 7 versus the Bengals. Before getting hurt, he was operating as Baltimore's secondary tight end, filling a complementary role relative to veteran starter Mark Andrews.

items.headline: Hill (groin) was a full participant in Tuesday's practice.
items.summary: After the Ravens estimated him as a limited practice participant Monday on their initial Week 9 injury report, Hill took every rep Tuesday to clear up any concern about his availability heading into Thursday's game against the Jaguars. Hill should serve in his familiar role as the Ravens' top passing-down back in Week 9, with Derrick Henry continuing to lead the way on the ground.

items.headline: Sarratt (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Bengals.
items.summary: Sarratt will be sidelined for six of the Ravens' first seven games of the regular season. His next chance to play is Week 8 against the Bills on Nov. 1, but it looks like the rookie fourth-rounder won't have a role in the offense unless another receiver misses time.

items.headline: Wester went without a target while playing six of the Ravens' 51 snaps on offense in Sunday's 36-10 loss to the Bills. He also returned three kickoffs for 71 yards and one punt for two yards.
items.summary: Though he remains locked in as the Ravens' top return man, Wester continues to see light playing time on offense. He hasn't logged double-digit snaps on offense since Week 3 and has been limited to four receptions for 44 yards on five targets through eight games.

items.headline: Randall (neck) wasn't activated from injured reserve Saturday and won't be available for Sunday's game against the Bills, Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Randall was placed on injured reserve to open the regular season due to a neck injury. He was cleared to return to practice Wednesday and logged three consecutive full sessions, but the Ravens will wait at least one more week before bringing him back from IR. The rookie fifth-round running back's next opportunity to make his NFL debut will arrive Thursday against the Jaguars.

items.headline: Reed signed with the Ravens' practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The quarterback's signing comes in the wake of Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley suffering thumb and toe injuries, respectively, during Sunday's loss to the Bills. Reed spent time with the Ravens during training camp and the preseason, and although he has yet to appear in an NFL regular-season game, he threw for 1,923 yards with a 21:9 TD:INT and added 108 rushing yards while starting all 10 games for the UFL's Dallas Renegades during the spring league's 2026 season. Baltimore's third-string QB, Joe Fagnano, is also dealing with an ankle injury and was limited during Monday's walkthrough.

items.headline: Cook rushed 21 times for 80 yards and a touchdown while catching two of three targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens.
items.summary: Cook gave the Bills some breathing room with a five-yard touchdown run in the third quarter to extend Buffalo's lead to 23-10. He was evaluated for a head injury later in the game but received clearance to return and notched one more carry after that point. After being held to 57 rushing yards without a touchdown by the Texans in Week 1, Cook has rushed for at least 75 yards and a touchdown in six consecutive games. Extending that streak won't be easy in Week 9 against Minnesota's elite defense on MNF.

items.headline: Davis rushed six times for 30 yards in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens.
items.summary: With the Bills throttling the Ravens and James Cook suffering a neck injury late in the game, Davis got some added run in the fourth quarter. If Cook misses any time, Davis would be the likely early-down replacement, with Ty Johnson sticking to his role on passing downs and four- and two-minute situations.

items.headline: Dortch went without a target while logging four of the Bills' 82 snaps on offense in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens. He returned one kickoff for 22 yards and three punts for 40 yards.
items.summary: Dortch has been serving as Buffalo's top return man throughout the season, but he continues to see limited involvement as a receiver. The 28-year-old hasn't played more than five offensive snaps in any of his seven appearances and has yet to draw a target.

items.headline: Johnson took four carries for four yards and caught all three of his targets for 19 yards during Sunday's 36-10 win versus the Ravens.
items.summary: In a game that Buffalo ran away with in the second half, Johnson's four carries were a season high, but he couldn't produce much on those rush attempts. Ray Davis actually saw more carries (six) in Week 8 and was more effective as a rusher (30 yards). As long as lead back James Cook is available, Johnson won't have much utility in most fantasy formats.

items.headline: Kincaid (chest) caught four of six targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens.
items.summary: Kincaid was questionable coming into the game due to a chest injury, but he managed to suit up and finished as the team leader in receiving yards. He made a 40-yard catch early in the fourth quarter and capped the following drive with a 23-yard touchdown catch. The streaky TE has returned to form with 11 catches for 124 yards and a touchdown over the past two games. Kincaid had just four catches for 52 yards over his previous three outings after starting the season with 12 catches for 225 yards and a TD through two games. Next up for Kincaid and the Bills is a Week 9 MNF clash with Minnesota's elite defense.

items.headline: Knox caught one of two targets for six yards in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens.
items.summary: It's a typical receiving line for Knox, whose main contributions come in the blocking department. Knox has nine grabs for 42 yards and one touchdown across seven appearances this season. He'd likely need multiple wideout and tight-end injuries to be a fantasy consideration.

items.headline: Palmer (hamstring) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Ravens.
items.summary: DJ Moore, Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman and Greg Dortch are thus available to handle Buffalo's wideout duties for the remainder of the contest. Palmer's next chance to see game action will arrive Nov. 9 against the Vikings.

items.headline: Shakir caught five of six targets for 64 yards in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens.
items.summary: Shakir initially appeared to get in the end zone for a six-yard touchdown early in the first quarter, but he was ruled out at the one-yard line after review. Josh Allen then punched in the one-yard touchdown two plays later. On the day, Shakir paced the Bills with his five grabs and tied for second on the team in targets, one behind DJ Moore. Shakir has yet to hit 100 yards in a game this season and has just one touchdown, settling in as a low-ceiling WR4 in fantasy, especially when both Moore and Dalton Kincaid are healthy.

items.headline: The Bills designated Shavers (knee) to return from the reserve/PUP list Wednesday, but he will not play against the Ravens on Sunday, Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network reports.
items.summary: Shavers has progressed enough in his recovery from a torn ACL to return to practice, and he was a limited participant in Wednesday's session. Shavers saw his role in the Bills' offense steadily increase over the course of the 2025 season before suffering his injury in the wild-card round against the Jaguars in January. His next opportunity to play is Week 9 against the Vikings on Monday, Nov. 9.

items.headline: Coker secured two of five targets for 37 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers' 27-19 loss to the Packers on Thursday. He also lost a fumble.
items.summary: Coker was having a forgettable night before he used his speed to turn a short Bryce Young pass into a 26-yard touchdown with just under six minutes remaining in the contest. Coker's fumble came on the last play of the game, as he lost the handle on the ball shortly after receiving a lateral from Tetairoa McMillan at the Panthers' 26-yard line. Coker is in the midst of a two-game downturn that unsurprisingly coincides with struggles on the part of Bryce Young, as the speedy wideout has just three receptions for 45 yards and Thursday's score in that span heading into a tough Week 9 assignment at home against the Broncos on Sunday, Nov. 8.

items.headline: Dillon (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday night's contest against the Packers, Darin Gantt of the team's official website reports.
items.summary: Dillon will be a healthy scratch for the second straight week as the Panthers go with Chuba Hubbard, Trevor Etienne and Anthony Tyus as their three options in the backfield. Dillon appears to have found himself far down the pecking order, and he is unlikely to be a major part of Carolina's future plans.

items.headline: Etienne posted six carries for eight yards, reeled in both targets for 17 yards and compiled 69 kickoff-return yards during Sunday's 43-13 defeat to the Buccaneers.
items.summary: Etienne made his second appearance of the 2026 campaign after missing the first four games due to an ankle injury. Although he was slightly more productive than he was in the Week 6 win over the Eagles, it was still an underwhelming showing overall. Etienne should continue to occupy the No. 2 spot on the depth chart. However, Chuba Hubbard is anticipated to nearly monopolize the touches out of the backfield moving forward, leaving sparse opportunity for anyone else.

items.headline: Evans gathered in both targets for 39 yards during Sunday's 43-13 loss versus Tampa Bay.
items.summary: Evans logged more offensive snaps than Darren Waller for the third consecutive contest. However, despite the increased involvement, it was another unproductive effort from the 23-year-old, who now has just eight catches for 105 yards in six regular-season games in 2026.

items.headline: King (coach's decision) is inactive but operating as the Panthers' emergency No. 3 quarterback against the Packers on Thursday night, Darin Gantt of the team's official website reports.
items.summary: King will once again serve as the team's emergency QB for the seventh game in a row. The rookie would only be eligible to enter the game if both starter Bryce Young and primary backup Kenny Pickett are forced out of the contest.

items.headline: McMillan brought in six of 11 targets for 57 yards in the Panthers' 27-19 loss to the Packers on Thursday.
items.summary: McMillan led the Panthers in receiving yards despite generating a modest total, and the second-year wideout has now fallen under 60 receiving yards in consecutive games for the first time this season. He does have at least six grabs in three of the past four games and a trio of double-digit target tallies on the season, so he continues to sport a formidable fantasy floor despite Bryce Young's current struggles. Carolina's air attack may have a tough time bouncing back in Week 9, however, as the stingy Broncos defense comes to town on Sunday, Nov. 8.

items.headline: Metchie recorded three receptions for 14 yards on three targets in Thursday's 27-19 loss to the Packers.
items.summary: Metchie took the field for 33 of the Panthers' 73 snaps on offense, placing him behind Tetairoa McMillan (65 snaps) and Jalen Coker (63) but ahead of Brycen Tremayne (19) and David Moore (zero) among Carolina receivers. Though he's now drawn at least three targets in five straight games, Metchie has found the end zone just once and is averaging 22.8 receiving yards per contest during that stretch.

items.headline: Moore didn't receive any playing time on offense and logged two snaps on special teams in Thursday's 27-19 loss to the Packers.
items.summary: After logging a season-high 13 snaps on offense a week earlier in the Panthers' blowout loss to the Buccaneers, Moore's playing time was contained to special teams while Carolina leaned exclusively on Tetairoa McMillan, Jalen Coker, Brycen Tremayne and John Metchie at receiver.

items.headline: Sanders (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday night's matchup with Green Bay, Darin Gantt of the team's official website reports.
items.summary: Sanders will be a healthy scratch for the sixth game in a row to open the regular season. Tommy Tremble and Darren Waller will operate as the team's primary options at tight end versus the Packers.

items.headline: Tremayne finished with an 11-yard reception on his lone target in Thursday's 27-19 loss to the Packers.
items.summary: Tremayne took the field for 19 of the Panthers' 73 snaps on offense, with his 26-percent share marking his lowest rate since Week 2. The 26-year-old appears to have been passed up on the depth chart at receiver by John Metchie, who logged 33 snaps Thursday and has now had higher playing-time shares than Tremayne for three straight games.

items.headline: Tremble hauled in one of two targets for eight yards during Sunday's 43-13 loss to the Buccaneers.
items.summary: Tremble had two touchdowns in the 25-14 win over the Eagles in Week 6. However, it was a different story in Week 7, with the 26-year-old catching just one pass for the second time this season. While Tremble could find the end zone again at some point moving forward, he likely won't be consistent enough to be considered anything other than a desperation fantasy option, especially while Darren Waller is on the field.

items.headline: Tyus rushed three times for 23 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 43-13 loss to the Bucs.
items.summary: With Carolina getting smeared on the scoreboard late in the game, the Panthers pulled their starters, and Tyus got some run on offense. He scored a 12-yard touchdown late in the fourth quarter. Tyus isn't even remotely on the fantasy radar while Chuba Hubbard is healthy.

items.headline: Waller corralled one of two targets for 11 yards during last Thursday's 27-19 loss at Green Bay.
items.summary: Waller has been hit or miss from a fantasy perspective this season, with two touchdown grabs in Week 2 in Atlanta and a 50-yard TD catch in Week 7 against the Buccaneers serving as the notable performances. Otherwise, he has one 50-yard effort in his five other appearances, sitting on a 15-209-3 line on 25 targets on the season. Waller next takes aim at the tough Broncos defense this coming Sunday.

items.headline: Brooks (core) was seen working off to the side during the Panthers' unofficial practice Tuesday, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: The Panthers haven't yet opened Brooks' 21-day practice window, but that might happen soon after head coach Dave Canales said Monday that the young running back would "potentially" be designated for return from injured reserve this week. Brooks hasn't played since Week 2 after undergoing core-muscle surgery, so he'll likely need to turn in multiple full practices before the Panthers are comfortable clearing him for game action. Once he's activated from IR, Brooks will likely handle a supporting role out of the backfield behind starter Chubba Hubbard.

items.headline: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said Monday that Legette (knee) will "potentially" be designated for return from injured reserve this week, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Canales noted that Legette still has some checkpoints he needs to hit in his recovery process before getting the green light to practice, but the third-year wideout appears to have at least progressed on some level since landing on IR on Oct. 3. Before getting hurt, Legette had served as the Panthers' No. 3 wideout during the first two weeks of the season and produced a 2-64-0 receiving line on six targets between those contests.

items.headline: Carlson reverted to the Bears' practice squad Tuesday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Carlson was elevated ahead of Chicago's win over Seattle on Monday and logged 10 offensive snaps, along with four special-teams snaps, without otherwise getting into the box score. It was his first game-day action of the season, so the veteran tight end is eligible to be elevated twice more. With Cole Kmet (knee) landing on season-ending IR in late October, Carlson could be called upon again in Week 9 against Tampa Bay.

items.headline: Johnson carried five times for 17 yards and added an 11-yard reception on his lone target in Monday's 34-17 win over the Seahawks.
items.summary: With Kyle Monangai (toe/thumb) inactive for a fourth straight game, Johnson continued to serve as the No. 2 running back behind D'Andre Swift. Unsurprisingly, Swift (27 carries for 69 yards and three touchdowns) handled the brunt of the work out of the backfield, with Johnson taking the field for just 14 of the team's 70 offensive snaps. If Monangai is able to make it back for Sunday's matchup with the Buccaneers, Johnson's playing time on offense could disappear entirely.

items.headline: Keenum (coach's decision) is inactive but will operate as the Bears' emergency third quarterback for Monday night's matchup against the Seahawks.
items.summary: Keenum will serve as the No. 3 QB for the third straight week, while Tyson Bagent slots in as the primary backup behind starter Caleb Williams. Keenum will only be eligible to enter the contest if both Williams and Bagent are forced out of the game.

items.headline: Loveland secured seven of nine targets for 65 yards and lost a fumble in the Bears' 34-17 win over the Seahawks on Monday night.
items.summary: Loveland continued his upward trajectory by tying Luther Burden for the team lead in catches and targets, and he finished second in receiving yards to Rome Odunze. The second-year tight end's fourth-quarter fumble was costly for the moment, however, as Loveland lost the ball at the Bears' 21-yard line following an eight-yard reception, and the turnover ultimately led to the Seahawks' final touchdown of the contest. Nevertheless, Loveland now has at least six receptions in four of the last five games, including three straight, and he's drawn 21 targets over the last pair of contests alone heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday night.

items.headline: Odunze brought in four of six targets for 87 yards in the Bears' 34-17 win over the Seahawks on Monday night.
items.summary: Odunze led the Bears in receiving yards on the night while finishing second in receptions and targets. The third-year wideout's catch and yardage totals both qualified as his second highest of the season, and Odunze now has 156 receiving yards over the last pair of contests for his most productive two-game stretch this season. Odunze is averaging a career-best 16.7 yards per catch and already has a career-high 14 receptions of 20-plus yards heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday night.

items.headline: Raymond finished Monday's 34-17 win against Seattle with two catches for 14 yards on three targets along with one rush for 39 yards.
items.summary: Raymond's most memorable contribution was a 39-yard dash on a third-down play early in the fourth quarter to take the ball down to Seattle's five-yard line and set up a D'Andre Swift touchdown. Though he didn't put up massive numbers, Raymond's 53 total yards were his most since Week 3 and represented more yardage than he had recorded over his previous four games combined. Raymond remains a shaky fantasy play given his recent numbers, and a Week 9 matchup against a Tampa Bay defense that has been pretty stingy on wideouts doesn't improve his outlook.

items.headline: Roush went without a target while playing 37 of the Bears' 70 snaps on offense in Monday's 34-17 win over the Seahawks.
items.summary: With Cole Kmet landing on injured reserve with a season-ending knee injury, Roush stepped into an increased role on offense, as his 53 percent snap share represented a season-best mark. However, the added playing time didn't translate to any involvement in the passing game, as Roush ran just 12 routes on the night. The Bears' frequent usage of two-tight-end formations should continue to prop up Roush's snap counts, but he's likely to be utilized mainly as a blocker when he's on the field.

items.headline: Chicago signed Scott from the practice squad to the active roster Tuesday.
items.summary: Scott was elevated each of the past three weeks, so this was a necessary move for him to be eligible to continue suiting up on game days. The 27-year-old has been providing depth at running back in the absence of Kyle Monangai (toe), who has been sidelined for each of the three contests that Scott has been elevated. With that said, Scott has yet to log an offensive snap this season, so he's unlikely to be a factor on offense in Week 8 versus Seattle even if Monangai is absent again.

items.headline: Gesicki caught four of six targets for 76 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 43-36 overtime win against the Titans.
items.summary: Gesicki was able to reach the end zone for the fifth straight game, connecting with Joe Burrow for a 25-yard score in the fourth quarter. The tight end's four catches and 76 receiving yards were both his highest totals since Week 1 versus Tampa Bay. Gesicki has now caught 17 of 24 targets for 241 yards and six scores over seven contests to open the regular season.

items.headline: The Bengals signed Grandy off the Vikings' practice squad Monday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
items.summary: Grandy spent the previous two seasons with Cincinnati prior to being a part of final cuts this past summer. With Tanner Hudson (pectoral) done for the season and Erick All going down with a knee injury Sunday against the Ravens, Grandy gives the Bengals another reliable tight end behind Mike Gesicki and Drew Sample.

items.headline: Meyers failed to catch either of his two targets in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Ravens.
items.summary: With Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins both fully healthy, Meyers played just 20 of 53 offensive snaps and ran 16 routes on Joe Burrow's 32 dropbacks. Outside of his 7-82-0 receiving performance in Week 4 against the Jaguars, Meyers has totaled six catches for 59 yards in the other five games.

items.headline: Perine rushed four times for 10 yards and caught his lone target for nine yards in Sunday's 43-36 overtime win over the Titans.
items.summary: The Bengals were chasing the Titans on the scoreboard much of the afternoon, and Chase Brown and Perine combined for just 16 carries, as Joe Burrow fired off 48 pass attempts. Perine is a touchdown-or-bust desperation RB3 in fantasy whose main value comes in the form of being Brown's backup. Cincinnati has been linked to a potential trade for a running back ahead of next week's deadline.

items.headline: Sample caught both of his targets for 24 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Ravens.
items.summary: Sample entered Week 7 with just five catches for 24 yards on six targets across five games, so he doubled his yardage total and secured his first touchdown with Sunday's performance. It goes without saying, but Sample isn't on the fantasy football radar.

items.headline: Tinsley (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Tennessee.
items.summary: Tinsley has played in each of the Bengals' last three games and has logged four catches on eight targets for 56 yards over that span. He will observe Sunday's contest from the sidelines, and his next opportunity to play is Week 9 against the Falcons on Nov. 8.

items.headline: Young went without a target while playing 19 of the Bengals' 74 snaps on offense in Sunday's 43-36 overtime win over the Titans.
items.summary: Though quarterback Joe Burrow set season highs in passing yards (462) and passing touchdowns (five), Young didn't see any involvement while the targets were highly concentrated among Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown. The fourth-round pick out of Georgia has held a bit role so far during his rookie season, recording two catches for nine yards on two targets through five appearances.

items.headline: Iosivas (thumb) is making good progress in his rehab, Mike Petraglia of CLNSCincy.com reports.
items.summary: Iosivas has been on injured reserve since Sept. 26 while recovering from a torn ligament in his left thumb that required surgery. The wide receiver is reportedly on track to be available to play in Week 10 against the Steelers, and he has an outside chance of returning one week prior against the Falcons in Spain on Nov. 8, per Petraglia.

items.headline: The Bengals placed Kattus (undisclosed) on their practice-squad injured list Tuesday.
items.summary: Kattus went undrafted in April and signed with Cincinnati as an undrafted free agent in early May. He didn't make the team's 53-man roster but was brought on to the practice squad Oct. 20. It's not clear what type of injury Kattus is dealing with, but now that he's on the injured list, he's not eligible to be elevated for the next four games.

items.headline: The Bengals signed Prieskorn to their practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: Prieskorn has bounced around between several organizations' practice squads over the past two campaigns but has yet to be elevated for a regular-season game. Most recently, he spent time in Carolina's training camp before being cut in late August. Prieskorn's signing was one of a flurry of moves by Cincinnati involving tight ends Tuesday, as Erick All (knee) was placed on injured reserve, Josh Kattus (undisclosed) landed on the practice-squad injured list and Cam Grandy was signed to the active roster.

items.headline: Bond went without a target while taking the field for eight of the Browns' 70 snaps on offense in Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers. He returned one kickoff for 26 yards.
items.summary: Since posting a 3-74-0 receiving line on seven targets in a Week 5 loss to the Jets, Bond has settled back into a muted role on offense. He's logged single-digit snaps in three straight contests, going without a target in each of those games.

items.headline: Boston caught six of 11 targets for 37 yards during Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers.
items.summary: Boston entered Week 8 having caught just four of 13 targets for 42 yards over the previous two games, so Sunday's output was a step in the right direction. The wide receiver's 11 targets were a new career high, and he ranked second behind tight end Harold Fannin (12) in the category versus Pittsburgh. Boston has now reeled in 26 of 53 targets for 409 yards and three touchdowns over the first eight games of the 2026 campaign.

items.headline: Concepcion caught three of four targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers.
items.summary: After a breakout game last Sunday against the Titans, which saw Concepcion record eight grabs for 129 yards on 10 targets, the rookie wideout came crashing back down against a divisional foe. Concepcion's four targets were a distant fourth on the team behind Harold Fannin (12), Denzel Boston (11) and Dylan Sampson (eight), and his four looks were good for just a 10.3 percent target share. Concepcion will try to rebound next Sunday against the Saints, but he's shown little upside, with zero touchdowns and just two games with more than 50 receiving yards.

items.headline: Corley went untargeted while playing 13 of 70 snaps on offense Sunday in the Browns' 27-6 loss to the Steelers. He returned one kickoff for 26 yards.
items.summary: For the fourth time in eight appearances, Corley logged double-digit snaps on offense, but the third-year receiver has yet to draw a target this season. He'll continue to provide most of his value to the Browns as a kickoff returner.

items.headline: Fannin brought in 10 of 12 targets for 154 yards in the Browns' 27-6 loss to the Steelers on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
items.summary: Fannin was one of the few bright spots for the Browns on either side of the ball in the ugly loss despite an early fumble, setting new career highs in receptions, receiving yards and targets. Cleveland's gradual shift to a pass-centric approach as its deficit grew was a boon for Fannin's production, and the second-year tight end now has a combined 16-245-0 line on 21 targets over the last two games alone. Fannin will aim to carry over the elite caliber of play into a Week 9 road matchup against the Saints next Sunday.

items.headline: Green (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback Sunday against the Titans, Kelsey Russo of the Browns' official site reports.
items.summary: Dillon Gabriel (back) is staying on IR, so Green will once again serve as the emergency QB3 behind Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders. As such, Green is not allowed to play Sunday unless both Watson and Sanders leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Jeudy did not catch his lone target Sunday in Cleveland's 27-6 loss to Pittsburgh.
items.summary: Quarterback Deshaun Watson had a relatively productive day with 324 passing yards (albeit without a score), but Jeudy was on the receiving end of only one of his passes. The veteran wideout logged his usual amount of playing time, notching a 60 percent offensive snap share to finish third among Cleveland wide receivers. It was the third time this season Jeudy has finished without a catch, but the other two instances were in Weeks 3 and 4, and he had been more involved of late, averaging 3.5 catches and 36.3 receiving yards over his previous four games. With that in mind, he could get back on track in Week 9 against a New Orleans defense that has been middle-of-the-pack against wideouts this year.

items.headline: McLaughlin turned five kickoff returns into 117 yards during the Browns' 27-24 win over the Titans on Sunday.
items.summary: McLaughlin played a key role in the Browns' Week 6 win over the Ravens, when he had nine carries for 41 yards and a touchdown while catching all four of his targets for 13 yards. However, his role on offense evaporated Sunday due to the returns of both Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson. McLaughlin figures to be limited to return duties moving forward unless one or both of Judkins or Sampson misses time.

items.headline: Ryan reverted to the Browns' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Ryan suited up for his seventh consecutive contest with the Browns, but his first as a practice-squad elevation. The seventh-round rookie played 12 special-teams snaps in the contest and did not appear in the box score. Ryan has two practice-squad elevations remaining before he will need to sign to the Browns' 53-man roster to suit up for regular-season games.

items.headline: Wallace recorded a three-yard reception on his lone target in Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers.
items.summary: The reception was Wallace's second of the season, after he previously notched a 12-yard grab in a Week 6 win over the Ravens. A key part of the Browns' special-teams coverage units, Wallace continues to handle a limited role on offense while the the team relies primarily on rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston and veteran Jerry Jeudy to fill out snaps at receiver.

items.headline: Guillory agreed to a contract to join the Browns' practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: Guillory had previously spent time in Baltimore's organization before being cut from the Ravens' practice squad in mid-October. He'll now have a chance to make an impression with the Browns in the hope of eventually being summoned for his first regular-season NFL action. Cleveland currently has a healthy wideout corps, so Guillory isn't likely to be elevated for Sunday's matchup against the Saints.

items.headline: Head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Monday that Ferguson (ankle) has a chance to play Sunday at Indianapolis, Jon Machota of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Ferguson hurt his ankle early in Sunday's eventual overtime loss to the Cardinals, eventually was ruled out and then diagnosed with a low-ankle sprain. Schottenheimer's comments one day later follow the general belief that players often are able to gut out such injuries, but how Ferguson fares in practice Wednesday through Friday will determine his availability for Week 9.

items.headline: Goodson took seven carries for 14 yards and caught both of his two targets for 19 yards during Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss versus the Cardinals.
items.summary: Dallas wasn't really able to get anything going on the ground in Week 8, totaling just 93 rushing yards on 39 carries. Just like the offense as a whole, Goodson found a bit more success in the passing game, and he posted his best receiving total since back in 2024. As long as starter Javonte Williams remains available, though, Goodson should stay in a change-of-pace role.

items.headline: Mitchell reverted to the Cowboys' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: With Luke Schoonmaker (groin) inactive and Jake Ferguson suffering an ankle injury in the first half, Mitchell played 31 offensive snaps behind Brevyn Spann-Ford. Mitchell actually got the scoring started, recovering a Javonte Williams goal-line fumble in the end zone. The tight end wasn't targeted in the passing game.

items.headline: Schoomaker (groin) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
items.summary: Schoonmaker was unable to practice Thursday nor Friday due to a groin injury that he sustained during Week 8 prep. He'll miss his first game of the regular season Sunday, and he'll aim to recover enough to return for Week 9 against the Colts on Nov. 8. Jake Ferguson, Brevyn Spann-Ford and James Mitchell will be the Cowboys' three active tight ends against Arizona.

items.headline: Spann-Ford caught four of five targets for 31 yards during Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss versus the Cardinals.
items.summary: Starting tight end Jake Ferguson logged only four offensive snaps before leaving Sunday's contest with an ankle injury, and Spann-Ford ended up playing a career-high 65 offensive snaps as a result. He ended up second on the team in targets behind CeeDee Lamb (11), and he could be worth a look as a streaming option in deeper formats if Ferguson is unable to suit up in Week 9 at Indianapolis.

items.headline: Turpin (ribs) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
items.summary: Turpin continues to work through a rib injury that he sustained in Week 6 against the Packers. The injury will sideline him for a second consecutive week, and his next chance to play is Week 9 against the Colts on Sunday, Nov. 8. Tyler Goodson and Jonathan Mingo will continue to serve as the Cowboys' returners on kickoffs and special teams in Turpin's absence.

items.headline: Williams churned out 56 yards on 24 carries and notched one catch (on two targets) for one yard during Sunday's 33-30 overtime defeat to the Cardinals.
items.summary: After failing to crack 20 rushes in any of the Cowboys' first six games of the season, Williams now has two such outings over the last two weeks. However, he averaged a season low in a single contest with 2.3 YPC on Sunday, and his TD streak also was snapped at five outings. Williams has a stranglehold on Dallas' backfield with 134 carries to date, while the rest of the team's RBs have combined for 37 through eight weeks. Williams will seek better results next Sunday versus the wayward Colts on the road.

items.headline: Adkins caught both of his targets for four yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 28-24 win over the Chiefs.
items.summary: The block-first tight end secured a two-yard score in the fourth quarter to pull the Broncos within three points, before they scored the eventual game-winning touchdown on the next possession. Adkins now has six grabs for 44 yards and a score on seven targets this season. He has no fantasy appeal.

items.headline: Dobbins carried the ball seven times for 13 yards in Sunday's 28-24 win over Kansas City.
items.summary: While the veteran RB got the start, by the end of the game Dobbins had fully given way to rookie Jonah Coleman, who wound up delivering 104 scrimmage yards on 15 touches and scored the game-winning touchdown. With RJ Harvey (knee) on IR, Dobbins will still have a role in the Denver backfield, but Coleman made a compelling case Sunday to become the team's new No. 1 back. Dobbins should at least be more productive in Week 9, even on limited volume, against a Panthers defense that's among the worst in the league against the run.

items.headline: Ehlinger (coach's decision) is inactive but will be the third emergency quarterback against the Chiefs on Sunday, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
items.summary: As the emergency QB3, Ehlinger is not allowed to play Sunday unless both Bo Nix and Jarrett Stidham leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Engram failed to catch any of his three targets in Sunday's 28-24 win over the Chiefs.
items.summary: Bo Nix targeted 10 different pass catchers on 32 total pass attempts, and it was rookie RB Jonah Coleman who led the team in receiving with a 4-63-0 line on five targets. Engram has just three catches for 15 yards over his last three games and isn't a recommended fantasy bet ahead of Sunday's date with the Panthers.

items.headline: Franklin failed to bring in either of his two targets in the Broncos' 30-16 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
items.summary: Franklin played 28 offensive snaps in Sunday's contest. Despite being on the field for 46 percent of the Broncos' offensive plays, the No. 3 option was targeted only twice and failed to catch either pass.

items.headline: Mims (ankle) practiced fully Thursday,Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
items.summary: Mims was a limited participant in Wednesday's session, but the wideout's full participation a day later sets the stage for him to be available Sunday against the Chiefs. The 2023 second-rounder has two catches in each of his last three games, with his Week 8 fantasy upside linked to the status of top WR Jaylen Waddle, who is managing a chest injury.

items.headline: The Broncos elevated Schrader from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
items.summary: The Broncos needed more depth in the backfield after placing RJ Harvey (knee) on injured reserve Saturday. It's the first time Schrader has been promoted to the active roster this season, and he'll operate as the Broncos' RB3 behind J.K. Dobbins and rookie Jonah Coleman for Sunday's game against the Chiefs. Schrader has appeared in two regular-season games -- both with the Rams -- since entering the league as an undrafted free agent in May of 2024.

items.headline: Sutton caught all four of his targets for 53 yards in Sunday's 28-24 win over Kansas City.
items.summary: For the fourth straight game, Sutton failed to see more than five targets, but his four grabs and 53 yards were both season highs. It's been a rough campaign so far for the 31-year-old receiver in an inconsistent Broncos aerial attack, and Sutton will take a 20-221-1 line on 37 targets through eight games intro a Week 9 clash with the Panthers.

items.headline: Waddle caught three of six targets for 39 yards and a touchdown and added a two-point conversion in Sunday's 28-24 win over Kansas City.
items.summary: Despite the fact that the wideout was playing through a chest injury, Waddle came up big when it counted, connecting with Bo Nix on a one-yard TD in the second quarter before snagging a two-point conversion in the fourth as Denver mounted a comeback from a 24-13 deficit. Waddle's 29-315-2 line on 51 targets through his first eight games as a Bronco is disappointing, but he still has time to pick up the pace beginning with a Week 9 tilt against the Panthers.

items.headline: The Broncos placed Badie (thumb) on injured reserve Saturday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Per Chris Tomasson of The Denver Gazette, Badie broke his thumb during the Broncos' 17-14 overtime win over the Seahawks in Week 6. Badie is required to miss at least four games, and the earliest he can return is Week 12 against the Steelers on Friday, Nov. 27. Jonah Coleman (ankle) was activated from injured reserve in a corresponding move, and if he's cleared to play Sunday, then he would slot in as the RB3 behind J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey.

items.headline: The Broncos placed Harvey (knee) on injured reserve Saturday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
items.summary: Harvey was already ruled out for Sunday's contest against the Chiefs, but now that he's on IR, the second-year running back will be required to miss at least the next four games. That means the earliest that he is eligible to return is Week 13 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Dec. 6. In Harvey's absence, the Broncos' backfield will be led by J.K. Dobbins and rookie fourth-rounder Jonah Coleman.

items.headline: Pancol was cut from the Broncos' practice squad Tuesday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official website reports.
items.summary: Pancol will return to the open market after inking a deal to join Denver's practice squad Oct. 27. The wide receiver's next opportunity will likely come as a member of another practice squad.

items.headline: Patterson was signed to the Broncos' practice squad Tuesday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official website reports.
items.summary: Patterson was cut from the Browns' practice squad Oct. 27, but he has now found another opportunity with Denver. With RJ Harvey (knee) on injured reserve for at least three more games, Patterson will provide the Broncos with another option in the backfield behind Jonah Coleman and J.K. Dobbins.

items.headline: The Lions signed Carter to the active roster Thursday.
items.summary: Carter last played for Cleveland in 2025, and he served as the team's main return man. The 33-year-old veteran is expected to do the same for Detroit after the season-ending knee injury to Tom Kennedy, per Eric Woodyard of ESPN.com.

items.headline: Saylors (neck) is not expected to practice Wednesday, Nolan Bianchi of The Detroit News reports.
items.summary: Saylor's neck injury is significant enough that Coach Dan Campbell felt comfortable declaring him doubtful to practice multiple days in advance. The kick returner/reserve running back couldn't return to Sunday's win over the Vikings because of the injury, and it remains unclear how long he will miss.

items.headline: St. Brown secured seven of eight targets for 46 yards and rushed once for 10 yards in the Lions' 19-15 win over the Vikings on Sunday.
items.summary: The star wideout suffered an injury scare in the first quarter on a play where an apparent 24-yard touchdown catch was overturned on replay, but St. Brown was able to return before long and finish the game. However, the suffocating Vikings defense, which St. Brown had enjoyed success against in the past, did a good job limiting him after the catch, even though he did finish with team-high reception and target totals. St. Brown now has failed to record a TD grab in four straight games, but he has at least seven receptions in each of those contests heading into a Week 9 road matchup against the Dolphins.

items.headline: TeSlaa caught one of his two targets for 10 yards in the Lions' 20-17 win over the Packers on Sunday.
items.summary: TeSlaa played 33 offensive snaps for the Lions in the contest, a 49 percent share of Detroit's offensive plays. However, TeSlaa saw a mere two targets for the second straight game after logging a season-high eight against the Panthers in Week 4, and Sunday's catch was his first since that game as well.

items.headline: Vaki rushed 11 times for 65 yards in Sunday's 19-15 win over the Vikings. He added one catch for five yards on one target.
items.summary: With Jared Goff struggling against the Vikings' blitz-heavy defense, the Lions dished out 34 carries to Jahmyr Gibbs and Vaki. It was Vaki's most extensive action of the season, and coach Dan Campbell said afterward that the Lions' RB2 took a "big step" and earned a lot of trust with his performance, according to Nolan Bianchi of The Detroit News. It's unclear if that will translate to more opportunities, but it's clear Vaki has cemented himself as Gibbs' backup and a quality bench stash in fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Williams brought in four of six targets for 70 yards and a touchdown in the Lions' 19-15 win over the Vikings on Sunday.
items.summary: Williams ended up leading the Lions in receiving yards on the day while checking in second to Amon-Ra St. Brown in receptions and targets. The fourth-year speedster also delivered the biggest catch of the day, recording a seven-yard touchdown grab with 4:35 remaining that proved to be the game-winning score. Williams has recorded all five of his touchdown receptions on the season within the last three games, and he has at least Sunday's yardage tally in three of the last four heading into a Week 9 road matchup against the Dolphins.

items.headline: Lions coach Dan Campbell said Friday that Pacheco (back) has a chance to return in late December, Justin Rogers of DetroitFootball.net reports.
items.summary: Pacheco has been sidelined for the entirety of the regular season to this point after undergoing back surgery in September. Sione Vaki has been working as the Lions' clear RB2, though Jahmyr Gibbs has been a true workhorse out of the backfield. If Pacheco does return at the end of the regular season, it's hard to envision him having a big impact coming off back surgery.

items.headline: NFL Week 9 latest intel, buzz questions, fantasy tips and trade deadline news
items.summary: What now for the Ravens without Lamar Jackson? What are people around the NFL saying about Justin Herbert's struggles? And what's the latest on the looming trade deadline?

items.headline: Golden brought in seven of 13 targets for 79 yards and a touchdown in the Packers' 27-19 win over the Panthers on Thursday.
items.summary: The second-year speedster finished second in receptions and receiving yards for the Packers on the night, while also leading the way in targets with a season-high-tying figure. Golden struck for his fourth touchdown of the season as well on a 24-yard scoring grab just after the two-minute warning in the first half, and the 2025 first-round pick now has at least six catches in four consecutive contests. He should remain busy in a Week 9 road showdown against the Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 8, one where New England shutdown cornerback Christian Gonzalez could spend the majority of his time on Christian Watson.

items.headline: Johnson (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday's game against the Panthers, Mike Spofford of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Johnson didn't suit up in the Week 7 loss to Detroit. The 23-year-old will be held out for a second consecutive contest, and he likely won't get back on the field moving forward if Josh Jacobs, MarShawn Lloyd and Pierre Strong are active.

items.headline: Kraft secured all six targets for 53 yards and a touchdown in the Packers' 27-19 win over the Panthers on Thursday.
items.summary: Kraft kicked off the scoring on the night for the Packers with his 12-yard TD grab in the first quarter, marking his third of the season and second in as many games. The athletic tight end also recorded the third-most catches and receiving yards on the night for Green Bay, and Kraft now has at least five receptions in four of the last five games. Kraft will take a 35-350-3 line on 49 targets into a Week 9 road matchup against the Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 8.

items.headline: Lloyd rushed three times for seven yards and brought in his only target for nine yards in the Packers' 27-19 win over the Panthers on Thursday.
items.summary: In his second game of the season, Josh Jacobs logged a total of 27 touches, leaving precious little work for any other back. Lloyd slightly outpaced Pierre Strong by two carries, but he still logged a season low in rush attempts. With Jacobs looking fully capable of handling a workhorse role moving forward, Lloyd may be destined for similar volume to Thursday's on most weeks as long as his star teammate is available.

items.headline: Melton caught one of his two targets for four yards and logged a 24-yard kickoff return in the Packers' 20-17 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
items.summary: Melton played 13 offensive snaps and 14 special-teams snaps in the contest. The No. 4 wide receiver remains a versatile depth option for the Packers, filling in wherever he is needed without garnering much attention.

items.headline: The Packers signed Owen from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
items.summary: Owen was elevated for the Packers' Week 6 win over the Cowboys. The wide receiver played just three snaps on special teams in the contest and has likely earned a roster spot as a depth option while Skyy Moore (ankle) and Jayden Reed (neck) are on IR. Owen could be involved in the return game against the Lions on Sunday.

items.headline: Smith (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday's game against the Panthers Mike Spofford of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Smith has appeared in each of the Packers' seven regular-season games. However, he will be a healthy scratch Thursday night, meaning Mark Redman and Josh Whyle will be behind Tucker Kraft on the depth chart.

items.headline: Williams caught three passes on as many targets for 47 yards and turned two carries into four yards during the Packers' 20-17 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
items.summary: Quarterback Jordan Love spread the ball around Sunday to eight different receivers, and Williams was one of five pass catchers to record at least three receptions. Williams finished fourth on the team in receiving yards, with two of his catches going for 27 and 20 yards in the first and second quarters, respectively. The second-year pro is cemented as the Packers' WR3 behind Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, and tight end Tucker Kraft also is in the mix for looks from Love. The Packers will head back to Lambeau Field and practice on a short week for Thursday night's game against the Panthers, whose defense ranks sixth in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game (195.7) and fifth in passing touchdowns allowed (seven).

items.headline: Packers head coach Matt Lafleur said Thursday it's "tough to say" whether Musgrave (neck) plays this season, Weston Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
items.summary: Musgrave has yet to return to the Packers since being placed on the PUP list prior to Week 1 of the regular season, and until the 26-year-old proves otherwise, he will likely continue to sit out. Tucker Kraft and Jonnu Smith will continue leading the charge at the tight end position.

items.headline: The Packers signed Miller to the practice squad Monday, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: By all accounts, both Jordan Love and Tyrod Taylor are healthy on the 53-man roster, so the signing seems to strictly be for organizational-depth purposes. Miller joins Kedon Slovis as quarterbacks currently on the team's practice squad.

items.headline: The Ravens signed Slovis off the Packers' practice squad Tuesday, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
items.summary: Slovis immediately becomes the healthiest quarterback on the Baltimore roster, as all of Lamar Jackson (thumb), Tyler Huntley (toe) and Joe Fagnano (ankle) emerged from Sunday's 36-10 loss to the Bills with injuries. Jackson is ticketed for injured reserve and Huntley is considered unlikely to play Thursday against the Jaguars, leaving Fagnano as the likely Week 9 starter after he was listed as a limited participant for Monday's walk-through practice. While the Ravens could elevate Austin Reed from the practice squad to provide another option at quarterback Thursday, Slovis -- who appeared in two games with Arizona in 2025 -- may be the preferred option to serve as Fagnano's top backup.

items.headline: Boutte caught one of two targets for 25 yards during Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss versus the Giants.
items.summary: Boutte played a season-low 18 offensive snaps in Week 7, trailing behind Nico Collins (34) and Xavier Hutchinson (31) and tying with Jaylin Noel (toe). Predictably, Boutte wasn't very involved in an inefficient passing game. As recent trade acquisition Marvin Harrison gets acclimated, Boutte's role probably will continue to shrink as the campaign continues.

items.headline: Hutchinson caught three of six targets for 17 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants. He added 12 rushing yards on two attempts.
items.summary: On a day in which C.J. Stroud targeted nine different players, Hutchinson tied Dalton Schultz for the team lead with six targets. Nico Collins led the wideout group with 24 routes, but Hutchinson tied Jaylin Noel (toe) for second at the position with 15 routes. In a receiver room that is running six deep on game days, none of these Houston wide receivers are reliably playable in fantasy outside of Collins.

items.headline: Jordan (foot) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Giants, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
items.summary: Jordan likely sustained his foot injury during Thursday's practice, but the tight end was quickly able to upgrade to a full participant in Friday's practice. Jordan is all set to suit up as a depth option at tight end in Sunday's contest.

items.headline: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said that Jordan was placed  on the practice squad injured list Wednesday due to a quadriceps injury, DJ Bien-Aime of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: With David Montgomery (groin) sidelined this past Sunday against the Jaguars in London, Jordan was elevated from the practice squad and made his season debut, working as the No. 2 back behind Woody Marks. Jordan took advantage of the opportunity, recording six carries for 43 yards and one touchdown and hauling in his only target for seven yards. Now that he's on the practice squad injured list, however, he must miss at least the next four games, meaning he won't be eligible to play again until Nov. 29 against the Ravens.

items.headline: How Gary Kubiak paved the way for his sons, Klint, Klay and Klein, in the NFL
items.summary: Klint, Klay and Klein Kubiak are all on their respective NFL journeys. But their father, Gary, helped each along the way.

items.headline: Marks rushed 19 times for 66 yards and caught his only target for 15 yards in Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants.
items.summary: Mark remained busy in the absence of David Montgomery (groin), handling 20 touches while no other running back got a touch for the Texans. Over the last three games, the first of which Montgomery left early and the last two of which he missed, Marks has recorded 247 scrimmage yards on 56 touches. Marks missed some action in the second half Sunday due to a leg injury but returned to the game. Houston's Week 8 bye will give both Marks and Montgomery a chance to heal up, and Houston would likely return to a backfield platoon in Week 9 against the Chargers if Montgomery's ready to play.

items.headline: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said Monday that he has "no significant update" on the status of Montgomery (groin) heading into a Week 9 matchup with the Chargers, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports.
items.summary: Prior to the Texans' Week 8 bye, Montgomery missed two straight games due to a groin injury and wasn't able to practice in advance of either of those contests. Ryans didn't offer much of an indication that Montgomery's condition has dramatically improved following the bye, with the coach noting that the running back will be evaluated throughout the week before a decision is made on his status for Sunday's contest. If Montgomery ends up being sidelined for a third consecutive game, Woody Marks would be in store for another turn as Houston's lead back.

items.headline: Moreau played 21 offensive snaps and nine special-teams snaps in the Texans' 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants on Sunday.
items.summary: Moreau did not appear in the box score of Sunday's game. The tight end's complete lack of offensive production was in stark contrast to his Week 6 two-touchdown effort against the Jaguars in London, and Moreau's week-to-week production figures to remain erratic while working behind clear No. 1 option Dalton Schultz.

items.headline: Ogunbowale didn't record an offensive touch or target in Sunday's 24-21 overtime loss to the Giants.
items.summary: Even with David Montgomery (groin) and Jawhar Jordan (quadriceps) injured and inactive, Ogunbowale played just seven offensive snaps behind Woody Marks' 54. Ogunbowale can continue to be ignored in fantasy football.

items.headline: Schultz caught five of six targets for 45 yards in Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants.
items.summary: The veteran tight end paced the Texans with his six targets, matching Xavier Hutchinson, as the duo saw one more than Nico Collins on a day when C.J. Stroud targeted nine different pass catchers. Schultz is still looking for his first touchdown of the season and has settled in as a low-ceiling fantasy tight end.

items.headline: The Texans signed Pitsenberger to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Undrafted out of Yale last spring, Pitsenberger signed with the Texans and spent the 2026 offseason with the team before suffering an ankle injury during training camp. Now healthy, he's back with the team via the practice squad. He ran nine times for 33 yards in one preseason appearance.

items.headline: Alie-Cox failed to haul in either of his targets during the Colts' 16-10 loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
items.summary: Alie-Cox led all Colts tight ends with 39 offensive snaps, but he could not connect with Daniel Jones on two pass attempts from the veteran quarterback. Alie-Cox and the other Indianapolis tight ends were operating in elevated roles for a second consecutive week due to the absence of Tyler Warren (groin). Alie-Cox's snap count would take a hit if Warren was cleared to return for Week 8 against Jacksonville.

items.headline: Allen caught all seven targets for 67 yards in Sunday's 42-7 loss to the Jaguars.
items.summary: The veteran wideout finished second on the team in targets, three behind Tyler Warren on a day Colts QBs attempted 30 passes. When on the field this season, Allen has been a consistent target-earner who runs routes that are friendly to quarterbacks in the short areas of the field. Not a big-play threat whatsoever at this stage of his career, Allen is averaging a career-low 9.0 yards per catch on 36 grabs this season. He has just one touchdown and is a low-upside WR4 for fantasy purposes headed into next Sunday's game against the Cowboys.

items.headline: Dulin (hamstring) was a limited participant in practice Thursday.
items.summary: That's two straight limited sessions to begin the week for Dulin after he missed the Colts' past two games due to a hamstring issue. The veteran wideout appears to be making progress in his recovery, as he didn't practice at all during Week 5 and Week 6 prep. Dulin's likelihood of returning for Sunday's matchup in Minnesota should gain clarity with the release of Friday's injury report and game designations.

items.headline: Giddens racked up 43 yards on six carries in Indianapolis' Week 8 loss to Jacksonville on Sunday.
items.summary: Giddens entered Sunday having not logged a snap this season, but he got an opportunity in the blowout loss and made the most of it, ripping off a pair of 12-yard runs on the way to a team-leading 43 rushing yards. However, it must be noted that he didn't enter until the game was far out of reach in the fourth quarter, so all of his production came in garbage time. Still, it was a meaningful performance by Giddens in the context of Indianapolis fielding trade offers for star RB Jonathan Taylor amidst a lost season. Should Taylor indeed be dealt, Giddens would immediately take on a more prominent role in the Colts backfield along with seventh-round rookie Seth McGowan.

items.headline: Gould (concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's Week 8 tilt against Jacksonville.
items.summary: Gould suffered a concussion in Week 6 against Tennessee and didn't play last Sunday versus Minnesota. Though he logged full practice sessions both Thursday and Friday this week, it appears he hasn't yet been cleared to suit up by an independent neurologist. As such, Gould will have to sit out another contest, which will primarily impact Indianapolis' plans for the return game.

items.headline: Leonard (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the Jaguars on Sunday, JJ Stankevitz of the Colts' official site reports.
items.summary: As the emergency QB3, Leonard is now allowed to see the field Sunday unless both Daniel Jones and Anthony Richardson are taken out of the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Mallory did not catch any of his three targets during Sunday's 16-10 loss to Minnesota.
items.summary: Mallory and the other Colts tight ends worked in larger roles offensively Sunday due to the absence of Tyler Warren (groin). However, the former's 21 offensive snaps ranked third behind Mo Alie-Cox (39) and Drew Ogletree (35), and Mallory could not connect with Daniel Jones, with the third and final pass that came his way resulting in an interception by Harrison Smith. Mallory has seen nine targets over his last two games since coming off injured reserve, but his role would shrink against the Jaguars in Week 8 if Warren is given the green light to play in that contest.

items.headline: McGowan rushed five times for 29 yards and returned four kickoffs for 103 yards Sunday in a loss to the Jaguars.
items.summary: McGowan's best run was a 16-yarder up the middle midway through the third quarter to take the ball to Jacksonville's three-yard line. That set up Indianapolis' only touchdown in the blowout loss. McGowan logged a modest 15 offensive snaps to starter Jonathan Taylor's 38, but the former outgained Taylor on the ground, 29-23. Meanwhile, DJ Giddens paced the Colts with 43 rushing yards on six totes. The big story, of course, is that the Colts are entertaining trade offers on Taylor, and if the star RB is ultimately dealt, McGowan and Giddens both figure to take on significantly larger roles, though it's unclear which of the two would become the starter. With that in mind, it's worth noting that Giddens didn't enter until the fourth quarter and racked up all of his yardage in garbage time.

items.headline: Ogletree (knee) is active Week 8 against the Jaguars.
items.summary: Ogletree will get the go-ahead to suit up despite failing to log a full practice all week and even missing Friday's session entirely. The ceiling is likely capped, however, as he'll be competing against the likes of Will Mallory and Mo Alie-Cox for tight end snaps following the return of starter Tyler Warren (groin).

items.headline: Treadwell caught one of two targets for 18 yards during Sunday's 42-7 loss to the Jaguars.
items.summary: Treadwell failed to record multiple receptions in a game for the first time since Week 3 against Houston. The wide receiver could be set to operate in a more prominent role if the team decides to deal fellow wideout Josh Downs prior to the trade deadline Nov. 10. For the time being, Treadwell doesn't figure to have much fantasy appeal Sunday against the Cowboys.

items.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Monday that Pierce (heel) will "most likely not" have his 21-day practice window opened in Week 8, Jake Arthur of Roundtable.io reports.
items.summary: A couple weeks ago, Pierce shed the cast that he had been wearing to protect his surgically repaired left heel, but the wideout looks like he'll remain limited to rehab work for at least another week before potentially making his return to practice. In Pierce's continued absence, the Colts will lean on Josh Downs, Keenan Allen and Laquon Treadwell to serve as their primary receiver trio, though none of the three have been consistent fantasy producers while quarterback Daniel Jones (4:7 TD:INT, 5.8 yards per attempt) has struggled mightily through the first seven weeks of the season.

items.headline: Boerkircher caught his lone target for a 31-yard touchdown in Sunday's 42-7 win over the Colts.
items.summary: The rookie tight end converted his long touchdown on a busted coverage, putting the Jaguars up 14-0 in the second quarter. Boerkircher entered Sunday with six grabs for 52 yards and a touchdown on eight targets across six games. He has minimal fantasy appeal outside of single-game DFS slates ahead of Thursday night's date with the Ravens.

items.headline: Cameron did not catch his lone target in a 42-7 rout of the Colts on Sunday. He returned one punt for six yards and one kickoff for 18 yards.
items.summary: Jacksonville didn't need to go to its air-game much given the easy win, and QB Trevor Lawrence threw just 14 passes. None of those went to Cameron -- his only target (which he didn't catch) came from backup signal-caller Quinn Ewers in garbage time. Cameron did log a season-high 52 percent offensive snap share, but game script didn't do him any favors in terms of production. With no catches in three of his seven games this season, Cameron doesn't make for an appealing fantasy asset.

items.headline: Hunter failed to catch his lone target in Sunday's 42-7 win over the Colts. He added five rushing yards on one attempt.
items.summary: With the Jaguars destroying their division rivals, Trevor Lawrence dropped back to pass just 17 times. Hunter's playmaking ability wasn't needed, as he logged just six offensive snaps. He'd likely benefit from a Brian Thomas trade ahead of next week's deadline.

items.headline: Lawrence completed 10 of 14 passes for 210 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions while rushing three times for 10 yards in the Jaguars' 42-7 win over the Colts on Sunday.
items.summary: Lawrence helped the Jaguars to a commanding 28-0 halftime lead with scoring strikes to Brian Thomas (12 yards) and Nate Boerkircher (31 yards), and he added a 25-yard TD toss to Bhayshul Tuten as time expired in the third quarter. Lawrence eventually gave way to Quinn Ewers late in the blowout win, but not before completing 71.4 percent of his passes and throwing at least three touchdown passes for the fourth time on the campaign. Lawrence now has 1,690 passing yards with a 17:4 TD:INT and has added 80 rushing yards heading into a Week 9 road matchup against the Ravens on Thursday night.

items.headline: Meyers (hamstring/ankle) was listed as a limited participant in Tuesday's practice.
items.summary: Though he's managing a pair of lower-body concerns coming out of Sunday's win over the Colts, Meyers' ability to practice in any fashion Tuesday bodes well for his chances of playing Thursday against the Ravens. However, Meyers may need to upgrade to full practice participation Wednesday to avoid taking an injury designation into the Week 9 contest.

items.headline: Rodriguez (hand) was listed as a limited participant in Tuesday's practice.
items.summary: Though he's been deemed a limited participant on both of the Jaguars' first two Week 9 practice reports, Rodriguez still looks to be in a better spot on the health front than Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot), who has yet to log any practice activity. If Tuten winds up being sidelined for Thursday's game in Baltimore, Rodriguez would be the favorite to lead the Jacksonville ground attack, provided he's not inhibited by his own hand injury.

items.headline: Strange caught both of his targets for 55 yards during Sunday's 42-7 win over Indianapolis.
items.summary: Strange was able to make it seven games in a row with multiple catches to open the 2026 campaign. The tight end tied running back Bhayshul Tuten for the team lead in receiving yards, exceeding 50 yards for the third time in the last four games. Strange has now reeled in 28 of 35 targets for 334 yards and a touchdown over seven contests this season.

items.headline: Allen caught two of three targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Broncos.
items.summary: The rookie wide receiver usurped Jalen Royals on the depth chart, operating as the clear WR3 behind Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy. Allen ran 22 routes on Patrick Mahomes' 44 dropbacks, but with both Rice and Worthy healthy alongside Travis Kelce and Kenneth Walker, there doesn't appear to be much juice to squeeze for Allen.

items.headline: Armstrong caught one of two targets for three yards during Sunday night's 20-3 loss to Seattle.
items.summary: Armstrong was signed to the active roster ahead of Week 7, and he was on the field for 56 percent of the team's offensive snaps. With Rashee Rice (hamstring) still banged up, it's possible that Armstrong operates in a similar role in Week 8 versus Denver.

items.headline: Gray caught both of his targets for 15 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Broncos.
items.summary: The Chiefs' TE2 caught a four-yard score in the third quarter, his first touchdown of the season. Kansas City uses plenty of 12 personnel, deploying both Travis Kelce and Gray on offense, but Gray handles more of the blocking duties. On the season, he has 14 grabs for 173 yards and a touchdown. There isn't much meat on the bone here for fantasy purposes.

items.headline: Johnson carried the ball once for 15 yards and caught all five of his targets for 128 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Broncos. He added 44 yards on his only kickoff return.
items.summary: The rookie running back flashed his explosiveness on a 73-yard catch-and-run in the second quarter that produced Johnson's first career NFL touchdown. He came into Sunday with a 9-109-0 line on 11 targets through six games, and his six touches were firmly behind Kenneth Walker's 25, but Johnson's breakout performance can only encourage Andy Reid to find more ways to get the ball in his hands. Johnson will look to build on this effort in Week 9 against the Jets.

items.headline: Nussmeier (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Denver, though he will be available as the team's emergency quarterback.
items.summary: Nussmeier is inactive for another contest. However, the signal-caller will be available if Patrick Mahomes and Justin Fields exit the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: The Chiefs signed Ott from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
items.summary: The Chiefs placed Brashard Smith (hamstring) on injured reserve Saturday in a corresponding move. Smith's injury leaves an opportunity for Ott. The undrafted free agent out of Oklahoma could make his NFL debut during Sunday Night Football as the Chiefs take on the Seahawks in Week 7.

items.headline: Watson reverted to the Chiefs' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's official transaction log.
items.summary: Watson was elevated to the active roster for a second week in a row ahead of Sunday night's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks. The wide receiver reeled in his only target for seven yards while playing five snaps on offense and two snaps with the special-teams unit. The Chiefs can elevate Watson one more time before the team would have to officially sign him to the active roster.

items.headline: The Chiefs placed Smith (hamstring) on injured reserve Saturday.
items.summary: Smith sustained a hamstring injury in Thursday's practice session and has promptly been transitioned to IR as he manages the issue. Running back Jaydn Ott has been signed to the active roster to be the No. 3 option behind Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson while Smith recovers.

items.headline: The Chiefs signed Carter to the practice squad Friday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Carter was cut from the Chiefs' practice squad Wednesday, but he's back in his old spot just two days later. He has yet to appear in a regular-season game in 2026 after in appearing in nine contests for the Falcons in 2025.

items.headline: Bech finished without a target or touch in Sunday's 38-33 Week 8 win over the Jets.
items.summary: Bech returned from a four-game absence due to a forearm injury and logged a 40 percent offensive snap share, but he didn't get any looks from QB Kirk Cousins. In fact, Cousins didn't go to his wideout corps as a whole very often -- 16 of his 26 targets went to tight ends, and another four went to running back Ashton Jeanty. Bech will look to get back into the box score Sunday in a Week 9 matchup in San Francisco.

items.headline: Benson (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Jets.
items.summary: The rookie sixth-rounder has suited up for each of the first seven games of the regular season, but with Jack Bech (forearm) cleared to play, Benson will be an observer from the sidelines for Sunday's contest. His next opportunity to suit up is Week 9 against the 49ers on Nov. 8.

items.headline: Mayer caught five of six targets for 53 yards in Sunday's 38-33 win over the Jets.
items.summary: Mayer's six targets were second on the team behind Brock Bowers' 10, and only Bowers (26) ran more routes than Mayer's 20 on Kirk Cousins' 27 dropbacks. The tight end has just one touchdown this season but has remained an integral part of Las Vegas' passing attack. He's already surpassed his 2025 catches and yards totals, posting 36 grabs for 351 yards through eight games this season. Mayer will be a fantasy TE2 for next Sunday's date with the 49ers.

items.headline: Nailor caught all four targets for 38 yards in Sunday's 38-33 win over the Jets.
items.summary: Both the catches and yards marked new season highs for Nailor, who entered Sunday with eight grabs for 75 yards and no touchdowns across six games. No team uses its receivers less than the Raiders, and Nailor accounted for four of the five targets between him and Tre Tucker against the Jets. Nailor has minimal fantasy appeal headed into next Sunday's road date with the 49ers.

items.headline: O'Connell (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Raiders' emergency third quarterback against the Rams on Sunday.
items.summary: O'Connell will only enter Sunday's game if both Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza must exit the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Thomas (shoulder) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Jets, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Thomas was a full participant in Friday's practice, which was enough for him to fade an injury tag for Sunday's road tilt. He has five catches on as many targets for 60 yards and one touchdown through seven regular-season games and will continue to serve as the Raiders' TE3 behind Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer.

items.headline: Thornton (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Jets.
items.summary: Thornton was activated from injured reserve Tuesday after fully recovering from a hamstring injury, but the second-year pro will be a healthy scratch for Week 8. In his absence, the Raiders will turn to Jack Bech, Cody White and Dareke Young to serve as the rotational wide receivers behind Tre Tucker and Jalen Nailor. Thornton's next chance to play is Week 9 against the 49ers on Nov. 8.

items.headline: Tucker did not catch his only target Sunday in the Raiders' 38-33 Week 8 win over the Jets.
items.summary: Despite quarterback Kirk Cousins throwing for 247 yards, Tucker had only one ball thrown his way. In fact, only one Raiders wideout -- Jalen Nailor -- had a reception, as Cousins targeted tight ends on 16 of his 26 passes. Tucker had caught either four or five passes in each of his prior six games and collected at least 97 receiving yards in three of those contests, though he finished below 45 yards in the other three. It's notable that he logged a season-low 52 percent offensive snap share against the Jets, but he should be in for better days ahead, beginning with a Week 9 matchup in San Francisco.

items.headline: White caught one of three targets for four yards in Sunday's 35-21 loss to the Rams.
items.summary: White has now posted back-to-back duds, totaling one catch for four yards on five targets across the last two contests. In an offense that doesn't often use three wide receivers on the field at once, White is pretty clearly behind both Tre Tucker and Jalen Nailor for snaps and routes. White ran just nine routes on Kirk Cousins' 48 dropbacks in Week 7.

items.headline: Runyon (foot) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jets, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Like during Week 7 prep, Runyon was a full participant in all three practice sessions for Week 8. However, the Towson product is not quite ready to be activated from injured reserve as he continues to recover from a foot injury.
